  1. Normalize. An event with a Records key is iterated record by record. Any other event is treated as a single record, which is how invoke-lambda submissions arrive.
  2. Extract (extract_record). An SQS record's body is JSON-decoded. An SNS record's Sns object is taken. If the result has a Message key, that is JSON-decoded too, which unwraps an SNS envelope delivered through SQS. If the result has no url but has Parameters.url_out, it is a Batch job description and is replaced by {"url": <url_out>}. A record that raises here is announced as RECORD_EXTRACT_FAILED, uploaded to the payload bucket's invalid prefix, and counted as a failure.
  3. Fetch. A {"url": "s3://..."} reference is replaced by the object it points at.
  4. Validate. A PayloadManager is constructed with set_id_if_missing=True, which builds a CirrusPayload, generates an id from the items and workflow name if the payload has none, and calls validate. A payload that fails is announced as NOT_A_PROCESS_PAYLOAD, uploaded to the invalid prefix, and counted as a failure. See Payload schema for what validation checks.

  5. Decide and start (PayloadManagers.process). The current state records for every payload in the batch are fetched with one BatchGetItem. Then, per payload:

  6. A payload ID already handled in this batch is dropped, with a DUPLICATE_ID_ENCOUNTERED event.

  7. A payload whose state is FAILED, ABORTED, CLAIMED, or absent, or whose process definition sets replace, is started.

  8. Any other state is skipped, with an ALREADY_PROCESSING, ALREADY_SUCCEEDED, or ALREADY_INVALID event.

    The full table is in The replace field and reruns.

Starting a payload is three steps. StateDB.claim_processing writes CLAIMED under a condition that fails if the record is already CLAIMED or PROCESSING, which is what stops two concurrent invocations from starting the same execution. The input payload is uploaded to <root>/executions/<payload_id>/<execution_id>/input.json. Then StartExecution is called with the payload inline, or with a {"url": ...} reference to the oversized prefix when the escaped JSON exceeds 120,000 bytes. Finally StateDB.set_processing moves the record to PROCESSING.

The execution name is deterministic: a UUID5 of the payload ID and the record's existing executions list. Reprocessing a payload therefore produces a new name only because the list has grown. If the state machine named in the process definition does not exist, the payload is recorded FAILED with that error and the message is not retried.

docs.title: Batch outcome
docs.text: If every record was handled, the invocation returns and SQS deletes the batch. If any record was rejected in steps 2 or 4, the invocation deletes the messages it did handle and then raises, so SQS redelivers only the rejected messages. After five receives they land on ${ResourcePrefix}-process-dlq.

docs.title: EventBridge trigger
docs.text: The EventBridge rule ${ResourcePrefix}-update-state-sfn-events matches Step Functions Execution Status Change events from aws.states whose stateMachineArn begins with arn:aws:states:<region>:<account>:stateMachine:${ResourcePrefix}- and whose status is SUCCEEDED, FAILED, ABORTED, or TIMED_OUT. The rule retries a failed invocation for up to 30 minutes and then sends the event to ${ResourcePrefix}-update-state-dlq.

docs.title: Parsing the event
docs.text: Execution.from_event reads the execution ARN, name, and status, and the input and output payloads embedded in the event. EventBridge omits the input when the escaped input and output together exceed 248 KiB, and omits the output as well when it alone exceeds that. The function raises if the input is missing, or if the status is SUCCEEDED and the output is missing, so an oversized output payload prevents the outcome from being recorded and the event ends on the dead-letter queue. Keeping payloads small avoids this; see Payload bucket: Oversized payloads.

docs.title: Status to state
docs.text:
Execution status Error type Recorded state Event SUCCEEDED SUCCEEDED SUCCEEDED FAILED stactask.exceptions.InvalidInput or cirrus.lib.errors.InvalidInput INVALID INVALID FAILED TimedOutError FAILED TIMED_OUT FAILED anything else FAILED FAILED TIMED_OUT set to TimedOutError FAILED TIMED_OUT ABORTED ABORTED ABORTED

The error type comes from the event's detail.error. The message comes from detail.cause: if the cause is JSON with an errorMessage key, that value is used, otherwise the raw cause. The two are stored on the record as <type>: <message> in last_error. When the workflow's Fail state does not use ErrorPath and CausePath, the event carries no cause and a fixed message saying so is stored instead. See Capturing errors. The cirrus.lib.errors.InvalidInput name is matched as a string for tasks built against an older library; no such class exists in this package.

docs.title: On success
docs.text:
For a SUCCEEDED execution the function, in order:

  1. Uploads the output payload to <root>/executions/<payload_id>/<execution_id>/output.json.
  2. Records SUCCEEDED and emits the event.
  3. Publishes each item in the output payload's features as one message to the publish topic, when CIRRUS_PUBLISH_TOPIC_ARN is set.
  4. Enqueues the next payload or payloads of a chain onto the process queue, when CIRRUS_PROCESS_QUEUE_URL is set. See Chaining workflows.

Step 2 runs before steps 3 and 4, so a failure to publish leaves the record SUCCEEDED.

docs.title: pre-batch
docs.text:
The function receives the state input, uploads it to <root>/tmp/batch/<payload_id>/<uuid>.json, and returns:

{"url": "s3://<bucket>/<root>/tmp/batch/<payload_id>/<uuid>.json",
 "url_out": "s3://<bucket>/<root>/tmp/batch/<payload_id>/<uuid>_out.json"}

The Batch job reads its input from url and must write its output payload to url_out. The workflow passes both through the Batch task's Parameters. See Batch tasks in a workflow.

docs.title: post-batch
docs.text:
The function receives the Batch task's output. When the job succeeded, that output carries the job's Parameters, which extract_record maps to {"url": <url_out>}. The function fetches the payload from that URL, validates it, and returns it to the state machine inline, or as a {"url": ...} reference to the oversized prefix if it exceeds the size limit, so the next task receives it the same way it would from a Lambda task.

When the job failed and the workflow's Catch routed the error into the input under error, the function reconstructs the job's own exception rather than passing on the generic Batch failure:

  1. It reads Attempts[-1].Container.LogStreamName from the error's Cause and fetches that stream's last event from the /aws/batch/job log group.
  2. It parses the line as <ErrorType>: <message> and raises an exception class created with that name, or UnknownError when the line has no type prefix.
  3. If the stream cannot be read, typically because the container never started, it raises an exception carrying the container Reason and attempt StatusReason instead.

A Cause without attempts, a container, or a log stream name raises with a message naming the missing field.

docs.title: api
docs.text: Serves the read-only HTTP API. It reads the state database, the data bucket's catalog.json, and the workflow metrics namespace, and never writes. See HTTP API.

docs.title: IAM roles
docs.text: Each function has its own role in cloudformation/core/functions.yaml. The grants are listed under Deployment contract: IAM grants.

docs.title: Payload bucket
docs.text: The payload bucket is the S3 bucket where Cirrus stores payload JSON: the input and output of every execution, and transient copies of payloads that are too large to pass inline or that failed validation. Together with the state database it is the record of a deployment's work. The state database says what state a payload is in; the bucket holds the payloads themselves.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
All bucket access goes through PayloadBucket in cirrus.lib.payload_bucket. PayloadBucket.from_env reads the bucket name from CIRRUS_PAYLOAD_BUCKET and the root prefix from CIRRUS_PAYLOAD_ROOT_PREFIX, default cirrus. It raises UndefinedPayloadBucketError when the bucket name is unset. Any bucket the functions can read and write serves. cloudformation/core/base.yaml creates ${ResourcePrefix}-payload-<account-id> and sets both variables on the functions, but a deployment built with other tooling can point them anywhere.

Every key Cirrus writes is under the root prefix, so the bucket can be shared with other content, or with a second Cirrus deployment using a different prefix, without key collisions.

docs.title: Key layout
docs.text:
Keys are split by how long the object needs to live:

  • <root>/tmp/ holds transient objects that are not needed once processing has moved on. A lifecycle rule is expected to expire them.
  • <root>/executions/ holds each execution's input and output payload, which the CLI and HTTP API resolve from state database records and which nothing expires.
s3://<payload-bucket>/
└── cirrus/                               # CIRRUS_PAYLOAD_ROOT_PREFIX
    ├── tmp/
    │   ├── oversized/<uuid>.json         # payloads too large to pass inline
    │   ├── batch/<payload_id>/<uuid>.json
    │   │                                 # input to a Batch job, written by pre-batch;
    │   │                                 # the job writes <uuid>_out.json beside it
    │   └── invalid/<uuid>.json           # messages process rejected
    └── executions/<payload_id>/<execution_id>/
        ├── input.json                    # written by process on claim
        └── output.json                   # written by update-state on success

The prefixes are attributes of PayloadBucket, computed from the root prefix at construction. Code that needs a key should call the class rather than build one.

A payload ID contains slashes, so keys under executions/ and tmp/batch/ fan out into several levels of S3 prefix, which makes every execution for a collection, workflow, or item set listable with an ordinary prefix query.

docs.title: Execution payloads
docs.text:
process writes the input payload to executions/<payload_id>/<execution_id>/input.json after claiming the payload and before starting the execution. If the payload arrived as a {"url": ...} reference, the referenced object is fetched and its content written, so the execution's input is always stored under this key. update-state writes the output payload to output.json beside it when the execution succeeds. A FAILED, INVALID, or ABORTED execution leaves only input.json.

<execution_id> is the Step Functions execution name, a UUID5 that PayloadManagers.gen_execution_arn derives from the payload ID and the record's existing executions list. Because a payload can run more than once, one payload ID prefix can hold several execution directories, one per attempt.

The state database record's executions list plus the payload ID is therefore enough to locate both files for any attempt. StateDB.dbitem_to_item fills input_payload_url and output_payload_url this way from the most recent execution, and the CLI's get-input-payload and get-output-payload commands download those URLs.

docs.title: Oversized payloads
docs.text:
Cirrus passes payloads inline through Step Functions and EventBridge, and EventBridge embeds an execution's input and output as escaped strings inside its event. To stay under that limit, PayloadManager.get_payload compares the JSON-escaped length of a payload with MAX_PAYLOAD_LENGTH, 120,000 bytes in cirrus.lib.payload_manager, and when the payload is larger uploads it to tmp/oversized/<uuid>.json and returns {"url": "s3://..."} in its place. This happens in process when starting an execution and in post-batch when returning a Batch task's output.

The reference is resolved wherever a payload is read: process at intake, CirrusPayload.from_event in the other functions, and stac-task's Task.handler in a task. A Lambda task with its own handler must resolve it itself. The Cirrus CLI's process and run-workflow commands also upload a payload larger than the SQS message limit to this prefix and enqueue a reference.

docs.title: Batch payloads
docs.text: pre-batch writes the state input to tmp/batch/<payload_id>/<uuid>.json and returns that URL as url together with url_out, the same key with _out.json in place of .json, where the Batch job writes its output. The <payload_id>/<uuid>.json form, rather than <uuid>/input.json, is kept for compatibility with earlier versions.

docs.title: Invalid payloads
docs.text: When process cannot parse a message or the payload fails validation, it uploads the raw message to tmp/invalid/<uuid>.json and puts that URL on the workflow event it emits. This is diagnostic storage, expected to expire with the rest of tmp/. A deployment that needs to keep rejected inputs should copy them elsewhere from a subscriber to the workflow event topic.

docs.title: Lifecycle and retention
docs.text:
The bucket the base stack creates has one lifecycle rule: objects under <root>/tmp/ expire after 10 days. That is long enough for a payload to survive retries and a manual rerun. An operator supplying their own bucket should add the same rule. Shortening it risks expiring an object an in-flight retry still needs. Widening it to cover executions/ deletes execution history, which breaks get-input-payload and get-output-payload for those executions.

Nothing Cirrus-managed expires executions/. A deployment that wants to bound its growth can add its own rule on that prefix, knowing that any execution whose payloads expire becomes unreadable through the CLI and API even though its state database record remains.

docs.title: Who reads and writes
docs.text: Caller Writes Reads process executions/.../input.json, tmp/oversized/, tmp/invalid/ {"url": ...} references from any bucket update-state executions/.../output.json Nothing; payloads come from the EventBridge event pre-batch tmp/batch/ post-batch tmp/oversized/ when the output is large tmp/batch/..._out.json Tasks tmp/batch/..._out.json from a Batch job tmp/oversized/ and tmp/batch/ Cirrus CLI tmp/oversized/ when enqueuing a large payload executions/ via state database records

docs.title: Payload schema
docs.text:
A Cirrus Payload is the JSON object that moves through a pipeline: the input items and the instructions for processing them. One payload starts one execution of one workflow. The shape is a GeoJSON FeatureCollection with a process field added:

{
    "type": "FeatureCollection",
    "id": "sentinel2/workflow-publish/S2A_1",
    "features": [
        { "<stac-item-1>": "..." },
        { "<stac-item-2>": "..." }
    ],
    "process": [
        { "<process-definition>": "..." }
    ]
}
Field Type Description id string Identifies the execution. See ID format. process generates one when it is absent type string Conventionally FeatureCollection. Not validated features array of Item The input items. Must be an array when present, and must be present when id is, since the ID is derived from it process array of Process definition Required, with at least one entry. Entries after the first describe a chain

CirrusPayload (cirrus.lib.cirrus_payload) subclasses stac-task's Payload, itself a dict. Its validate method runs stac-task's validation and then Cirrus's own:

  • stac-task reads process, features, and the process definition's workflow_options, tasks, upload_options, collection_matchers, and collection_options, raising TypeError when any has the wrong type, and raises ValueError when both collection_matchers and the legacy upload_options.collections are set.
  • Cirrus requires process to be a non-empty array, process[0] to have a workflow, and id to match the ID format.

Validation stops at structure. Whether the items are usable is for tasks to decide: a task that cannot process its input raises stactask.exceptions.InvalidInput, which update-state records as INVALID.

docs.title: ID format
docs.text:
id must match <collections>/workflow-<workflow>/<itemids>, the regular expression PAYLOAD_ID_REGEX in cirrus.lib.utils: (?P<collections>.+)/workflow-(?P<workflow>[^/]+)/(?P<itemids>.+). <workflow> must equal the process definition's workflow for the state database key to resolve.

When a payload has no id, CirrusPayload.set_id builds one. process does this on intake, and so does cirrus payload get-id:

  • <collections> is the process definition's collections field if set, otherwise the sorted, /-joined set of collection values across features, or none when no item has one.
  • <itemids> is the sorted, /-joined set of item id values.

Because the same items through the same workflow always produce the same ID, the ID is what makes processing idempotent. Two submissions differing only in process definition parameters are the same payload to Cirrus.

Workflow names must not contain underscores

The state database joins <collections> and <workflow> with an underscore for its partition key and splits on the last underscore to recover them. A collections segment may contain underscores; a workflow name may not, or lookups for that payload resolve the wrong key. See State database: Key schema.

docs.title: Item
docs.text:
An input item is a JSON object. Cirrus requires only that it have an id:

Field Type Description id string Required

Items are ordinarily STAC Items, which lets tasks work across data sources. A workflow whose job is to create STAC metadata can take partial items as input, for example a stub carrying only the URLs a task needs to build the real item:

{
    "features": [
        {
            "id": "tiles-15-V-WG-2022-3-21-0",
            "assets": {
                "tileInfo": {
                    "href": "https://roda.sentinel-hub.com/sentinel-s2-l2a/tiles/15/V/WG/2022/3/21/0/tileInfo.json"
                },
                "productInfo": {
                    "href": "https://roda.sentinel-hub.com/sentinel-s2-l2a/tiles/15/V/WG/2022/3/21/0/productInfo.json"
                },
                "metadata": {
                    "href": "https://roda.sentinel-hub.com/sentinel-s2-l2a/tiles/15/V/WG/2022/3/21/0/metadata.xml"
                }
            }
        }
    ]
}

The output of a workflow should be complete STAC Items, since that is what the publish topic's subscribers expect. Cirrus does not check.

docs.title: Process definition
docs.text:
The first element of process is the definition for the current execution.

Field Type Description workflow string Required. The workflow to run. No underscores collections string Overrides the <collections> segment of a generated id replace boolean Run even if the payload's current state would otherwise skip it. See below workflow_options object Parameters passed to every task in the workflow tasks object Per-task parameters, keyed by task name. See tasks upload_options Upload options How a task uploads and publishes item assets collection_options object Per-collection overrides, keyed by collection name. A {"<collection>": {"upload_options": {...}}} entry replaces upload_options for items in that collection collection_matchers array Rules assigning each output item's collection. See Assigning output collections chain_filter string JSONPath filter on the previous execution's output items. Chaining only; see Chaining workflows

docs.title: The replace field and reruns
docs.text:
Whether a submitted payload starts an execution or is skipped depends on its current state database record and on replace. The decision is made in two places:

  1. PayloadManagers.process (cirrus.lib.payload_manager), called by the process function, reads the record and computes _replace = replace or process_definition.get("replace", False), where the first replace is a method argument the CLI's migration tooling can pass. A payload runs when its state is FAILED, ABORTED, CLAIMED, or absent, or when _replace is true. Otherwise it is skipped and an ALREADY_* workflow event is emitted.
  2. StateDB.claim_processing then writes CLAIMED under a DynamoDB condition that fails when the record is already CLAIMED or PROCESSING. This closes the race between two concurrent submissions of the same payload, and replace cannot bypass it.
Current state Without replace With replace: true no record Runs Runs CLAIMED Runs, against the execution already reserved in the record Same PROCESSING Skipped Skipped. The condition blocks it regardless of replace SUCCEEDED Skipped Runs FAILED Runs Runs INVALID Skipped Runs ABORTED Runs Runs

Each run appends a new execution ARN to the record's executions list, so a rerun payload accumulates entries and the most recent one is the one commands resolve to. See State database: Fields.

get-input-payloads --rerun and Deployment.yield_input_payloads(rerun=True) set replace: true on process[0] of each payload they return, which is how bulk reruns get these semantics without editing payloads by hand.

docs.title: tasks
docs.text: tasks maps task names to parameter objects. A task built on stac-task reads Task.parameters, which merges workflow_options with the entry under its own name, the task's entry winning on conflicts. Each task documents the parameters it reads.

docs.title: Upload options
docs.text:
upload_options controls how a stac-task task uploads item assets, through Task.upload_item_assets_to_s3 and stac-task's upload_item_assets_to_s3 in stactask.asset_io.

Field Type Description path_template string Template for the S3 location of uploaded assets. Must resolve to an s3:// URL; stac-task's default ${collection}/${id} has no bucket and fails at upload public_assets array of strings, or "ALL" Asset keys to upload with a public-read ACL, or every asset headers object Extra arguments passed to the S3 upload, such as CacheControl s3_urls boolean Return s3:// URLs for uploaded assets instead of HTTPS URLs. Default false

The uploader takes each asset whose href is an existing local file, uploads it to <path_template>/<file name> with ContentType set from the asset's type, and rewrites the href. Assets whose href is not a local path are left unchanged.

docs.title: path_template
docs.text:
The template is resolved by pystac's LayoutTemplate against the item. A ${name} variable resolves, in order, against the item's own attributes, its properties, and its extra_fields, with these special names:

Variable Value date The date part of the item's datetime, or start_datetime when datetime is null year, month, day Parts of the same date collection The item's collection ID any property For example ${mgrs:utm_zone}

A template of s3://my-data-bucket/${collection}/${year}/${id} places an item's assets under its collection and year.

docs.title: Assigning output collections
docs.text:
collection_matchers assigns each output item's collection before the payload is returned. stac-task's Task.handler evaluates the matchers in order per item after process returns, and the first match wins:

{
    "workflow": "my-workflow",
    "collection_matchers": [
        {
            "type": "jsonpath",
            "collection_name": "landsat-derived",
            "pattern": "$[?(@.id =~ 'LC08.*')]"
        },
        {
            "type": "catch_all",
            "collection_name": "other-products"
        }
    ]
}

A jsonpath matcher assigns collection_name to items matching its pattern, a JSONPath expression evaluated against the item. A catch_all matcher matches every item and belongs last. An item matching no matcher keeps its existing collection.

The older form, upload_options.collections, maps a collection name to a JSONPath expression. stac-task warns that it is deprecated and rejects a payload that sets both.

docs.title: Publish topic
docs.text:
The publish topic is where a Cirrus deployment's output leaves it. When an execution succeeds, update-state publishes every item in the output payload's features to this SNS topic, one message per item. Anything downstream, a STAC API ingest, a feeder for another pipeline, an archive, subscribes here.

The reference templates create the topic as ${ResourcePrefix}-publish in cloudformation/core/base.yaml and pass its ARN to update-state as CIRRUS_PUBLISH_TOPIC_ARN. When that variable is unset, nothing is published.

docs.title: When items are published
docs.text: Publishing happens after the state database records SUCCEEDED and the output payload is uploaded, and only when the execution produced an output payload. A FAILED, INVALID, or ABORTED execution publishes nothing. Items are published as the final task returned them; Cirrus does not validate them as STAC. Messages are sent in batches of up to ten with PublishBatch, and a batch publish failure leaves the record SUCCEEDED, so a subscriber cannot assume it saw every succeeded execution's items.

docs.title: Message body
docs.text: The message body is the item's JSON, unchanged from the output payload. A subscriber that wants the whole output payload rather than one item at a time reads it from the payload bucket instead; the execution's output.json URL is on the state database record and on the SUCCEEDED workflow event.

docs.title: Message attributes
docs.text:
cirrus.lib.utils.build_item_sns_attributes sets these attributes on each message, each only when the item has the field it comes from. They exist so a subscription filter policy can select items without parsing bodies.

Attribute Type Source collection String The item's collection bbox.ll_lon, bbox.ll_lat, bbox.ur_lon, bbox.ur_lat Number The four values of the item's bbox datetime String properties.datetime start_datetime String properties.start_datetime, or properties.datetime when the former is absent end_datetime String properties.end_datetime, or properties.datetime when the former is absent cloud_cover Number properties.eo:cloud_cover status String created when properties.created equals properties.updated, updated when they differ. Absent when either field is missing

That is ten attributes at most, which is the limit SNS enforces for delivery to an SQS queue with raw message delivery.

docs.title: Subscribing
docs.text:
An SQS queue is the usual subscriber, since it buffers items for a consumer that processes them in its own time. A filter policy on the subscription narrows what the queue receives. To receive only items from one collection with cloud cover under 20 percent:

{
  "collection": ["sentinel-2-l2a"],
  "cloud_cover": [{"numeric": ["<", 20]}]
}

With raw message delivery enabled on the subscription, the queue receives the item JSON as the message body and the attributes as SQS message attributes. Without it, SNS wraps the item in its delivery envelope, with the item under Message and the attributes under MessageAttributes.

A feeder that builds a new payload from each published item is how one pipeline triggers another without chaining, and the publish topic is where a workflow event subscriber should not look for output: workflow events carry state changes and payload URLs, not items.

docs.title: State database
docs.text:
The state database is a DynamoDB table with one record per payload ID. It is what stops the same payload from running twice, records how each execution ended, and lets the CLI and HTTP API answer what happened to a payload. cloudformation/core/base.yaml creates it as ${ResourcePrefix}-state with on-demand billing. All access goes through StateDB in cirrus.lib.statedb, which reads the table name from CIRRUS_STATE_DB and also needs CIRRUS_PAYLOAD_BUCKET, because it builds payload URLs from records.

Who writes and reads it:

  • process reads the current state of each incoming payload, claims it, and moves it to PROCESSING.
  • update-state writes the terminal state and error.
  • api reads records and counts.
  • The Cirrus CLI reads records and resolves payload IDs to executions and stored payloads.

docs.title: Key schema
docs.text:
Index Partition key Sort key Table collections_workflow itemids state_updated GSI collections_workflow state_updated updated GSI collections_workflow updated

Both indexes project all attributes. The key is derived from the payload ID <collections>/workflow-<workflow>/<itemids>: StateDB.payload_id_to_key splits on /workflow-, then splits the remainder on its first /, and joins collections and workflow with an underscore. The reverse split, split_collections_workflow, cuts on the last underscore, which is why a workflow name may not contain one while a collections segment may. See ID format.

StateDB.query always conditions on collections_workflow and picks the index from the filters: a state filter uses the state_updated index with a begins_with on the state name, or a between on <state>_<start> and <state>_<now> when since is also given; since alone uses the updated index; neither uses the table, sorted by itemids. An error_begins_with filter is applied as a DynamoDB filter expression on last_error after the key condition.

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
The raw record, as get-state returns it:

Field Type Written by Notes collections_workflow string every state change Partition key, <collections>_<workflow> itemids string every state change Sort key, the item-ID segment of the payload ID state_updated string every state change <STATE>_<isotimestamp>, for example PROCESSING_2026-01-01T00:00:00+00:00. The current state is the prefix updated string every state change ISO timestamp of the latest change created string first change only Set with if_not_exists, never overwritten executions list of strings claim_processing Execution ARNs, appended on each claim, so a rerun payload accumulates entries claimed_at string claim_processing Timestamp of the latest claim last_error string set_failed, set_invalid <error type>: <message>. Removed by the next claim outputs list of strings set_outputs, set_succeeded Not written by any framework code path in this version; update-state calls set_succeeded without it. The methods remain for library callers. Removed by the next claim

StateDB.dbitem_to_item, used by get_item, get_items, the query and get-input-payloads commands, and the HTTP API, returns a converted record instead:

Field Notes payload_id Rebuilt from the key collections, workflow Split out of collections_workflow items The itemids value under a different name state The prefix of state_updated created, updated Copied input_payload_url S3 URL of the most recent execution's input payload, or null if there is no execution yet output_payload_url S3 URL of the output payload, or null unless state is SUCCEEDED executions Each ARN converted to a Step Functions console URL. Present only when the record has executions outputs, last_error, claimed_at Copied when present

to_current adds catid and catalog as aliases of payload_id and input_payload_url. They exist for cirrus-dashboard and are not part of the schema; new code should read the unaliased fields.

docs.title: States
docs.text:
StateEnum in src/cirrus/lib/enums.py:

State Meaning CLAIMED An execution is reserved for the payload and its ARN recorded, but the execution has not been confirmed as started PROCESSING The execution is running SUCCEEDED The execution succeeded FAILED The execution failed or timed out, or process could not start it INVALID A task raised InvalidInput. The payload will not succeed without modification and is skipped on resubmission unless replace is set ABORTED The execution was stopped

CLAIMED exists to close a race. claim_processing sets it under a condition expression that fails if the record is already CLAIMED or PROCESSING, so two invocations of process holding the same payload cannot both start an execution. set_processing then moves the record to PROCESSING under a condition that it is currently CLAIMED. Which states a resubmitted payload runs from is defined in The replace field and reruns.

docs.title: Reading and deleting records
docs.text:
The CLI's get-state, query, and get-input-payloads commands read the table; see Common workflows. The HTTP API serves the same records and per-state counts.

Deleting a record is not part of normal operation. StateDB.delete_item(payload_id) removes one by payload ID.

docs.title: Workflow events
docs.text:
A workflow event records a decision the process or update-state function made about one payload: claimed, started, skipped, rejected, or finished in a terminal state. Events are emitted by WorkflowEventManager (cirrus.lib.events), which each function constructs once per invocation. The methods that emit the started and terminal events also write the state database record, so the event stream and the state database agree by construction.

Events are not states. Several event types record a skip or rejection that leaves the state database untouched, and TIMED_OUT is an event type only: the state database records a timed-out execution as FAILED.

docs.title: Event types
docs.text:
WFEventType in src/cirrus/lib/enums.py defines the event types. The emit sites are cirrus.lib.payload_manager for the process function and src/cirrus/lambda_functions/update_state.py for update-state.

Event type Emitted by When CLAIMED_PROCESSING process StateDB.claim_processing succeeded. A Step Functions execution is reserved for the payload but not yet started. STARTED_PROCESSING process The execution was started and the record moved from CLAIMED to PROCESSING. ALREADY_PROCESSING process The payload was skipped because its record is PROCESSING. ALREADY_SUCCEEDED process Skipped because the record is SUCCEEDED and the process definition does not set replace. ALREADY_INVALID process Skipped because the record is INVALID and replace is not set. ALREADY_CLAIMED none Defined in the enum, but no current code path emits it. A payload whose record is CLAIMED is run against its pending execution rather than skipped. DUPLICATE_ID_ENCOUNTERED process The same payload ID appeared more than once in the batch one invocation received. The later copy is dropped. RECORD_EXTRACT_FAILED process No payload could be parsed from an incoming message. The raw message is uploaded to the payload bucket's invalid prefix, and payload_id is unknown. NOT_A_PROCESS_PAYLOAD process A payload was parsed but CirrusPayload.validate rejected it. The message is uploaded to the invalid prefix. FAILED update-state, process An execution ended FAILED with an error type that is neither an InvalidInput class nor TimedOutError. Also emitted by process when starting the execution fails, for example because the named state machine does not exist. TIMED_OUT update-state Execution status TIMED_OUT, or status FAILED with error type TimedOutError. INVALID update-state Execution status FAILED with error type stactask.exceptions.InvalidInput, or the name cirrus.lib.errors.InvalidInput, which is matched as a string for tasks built against older libraries. SUCCEEDED update-state Execution status SUCCEEDED. ABORTED update-state Execution status ABORTED.

RECORD_EXTRACT_FAILED and NOT_A_PROCESS_PAYLOAD both mean process rejected a message before any workflow could start. The first fires when the message itself cannot be turned into a payload object, the second when a payload object was built but failed validation. See Lambda functions: process for the intake sequence.

docs.title: Event fields
docs.text:
WorkflowEvent carries these fields. The serialized message omits any field that is unset, and replaces execution_arn with execution, the Step Functions console URL for that ARN.

Field Set on event_type Every event. payload_id Every event. unknown on RECORD_EXTRACT_FAILED, and on NOT_A_PROCESS_PAYLOAD when the parsed object has no id. isotimestamp Every event. UTC, ISO 8601. input_payload_url STARTED_PROCESSING, most ALREADY_* skips, DUPLICATE_ID_ENCOUNTERED, and the terminal events. On the two rejection events it is the URL of the uploaded raw message under the invalid prefix. Never set on CLAIMED_PROCESSING, which fires before the input payload is uploaded. output_payload_url SUCCEEDED, and ALREADY_SUCCEEDED. execution STARTED_PROCESSING and the terminal events. error FAILED, TIMED_OUT, INVALID, and the two rejection events. For terminal events the value is <error type>: <message> as extracted by update-state.

docs.title: Destinations
docs.text: WorkflowEventManager.announce sends each event to up to two destinations. Both are optional and independently configured by environment variables that cloudformation/core/functions.yaml sets on the process and update-state functions.

docs.title: Workflow event topic
docs.text:
When CIRRUS_WORKFLOW_EVENT_TOPIC_ARN is set, events are published to that SNS topic. The reference templates create it as ${ResourcePrefix}-workflow-event in cloudformation/core/base.yaml. Publishes are batched, up to ten per request, and flushed when the invocation ends.

The message body is the serialized event. Message attributes carry event_type, and error when the event has one. When the payload ID parses, they also carry workflow and collections. A subscription filter policy on these attributes can select, for example, only FAILED events for one workflow.

docs.title: CloudWatch log group and metrics
docs.text:
When CIRRUS_WORKFLOW_LOG_GROUP is set, WorkflowMetricLogger writes each event as one JSON log line, immediately, to a log stream named workflow-metrics-<uuid> that it creates per invocation. The line holds event, workflow, source (the collections segment of the payload ID), and execution_arn. A payload ID that does not match the ID format is logged with workflow set to could not parse and source set to the raw ID.

The metrics stack (cloudformation/core/metrics.yaml, created when the main stack's EnableWorkflowMetrics parameter is true, its default) provides:

Resource Name Notes Log group ${ResourcePrefix}-workflow-event-metrics One-day retention. Metric filter all_workflows_by_event Namespace ${ResourcePrefix}-workflow, dimension event, value 1 per line. Metric filter a_workflow_by_event Same namespace, dimensions event and workflow.

The main stack passes the log group name to process and update-state as CIRRUS_WORKFLOW_LOG_GROUP and the namespace to api as CIRRUS_WORKFLOW_METRIC_NAMESPACE, which WorkflowMetricReader uses to serve the HTTP API's /stats endpoint. When EnableWorkflowMetrics is false, both variables are empty strings, no events are logged, and /stats returns 404 unless the deprecated Timestream path below is configured.

docs.title: Timestream event database, deprecated
docs.text: EventDB (cirrus.lib.eventdb) writes to an Amazon Timestream table named by CIRRUS_EVENT_DB_AND_TABLE as DATABASE|TABLE. No template in cloudformation/ sets that variable. When it is set, WorkflowEventManager emits a DeprecationWarning at construction and writes one record for STARTED_PROCESSING and for each terminal event. Claims, skips, duplicates, and rejections are not written. The record's measure value is the state name, except that SUCCEEDED is written as COMPLETED and TIMED_OUT as INVALID. The /stats endpoint reads Timestream only when CloudWatch metrics are disabled.

docs.title: Reading events
docs.text:
• Subscribe a queue, function, or email endpoint to the workflow event topic.
  • Query the ${ResourcePrefix}-workflow metrics namespace directly in CloudWatch, or build alarms on it. See Monitoring.
  • Call the HTTP API's /stats endpoint for daily and hourly counts by state.

The Cirrus CLI has no command that reads events.
